correctness.rationale: The upper bound counts one-symbol outputs with multiplicities one and two and bounds total constant-weight words; the only n=3/list-2 exception is a triple collision at output 11. The construction uses all adjacent pairs and a degree-bounded graph encoding extra words. Three-zero-insertion superwords exhaust each weight-two output. Graphs with the required edge count exist by elementary circular-offset constructions, and the list-2 matching avoids every triple. The standalone checker has independently reproduced all asserted test cases; finite runs are not substitutes for the all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: List-decodable deletion codes are an active coding-theory topic. This theorem exactly resolves the natural first nontrivial constant-weight slice for every blocklength and every list size >=2, identifies a sharp exceptional boundary, and gives a structural equivalence to near-regular graph packing. It supplies interpretable exact benchmarks and an explicit code family, not arbitrary short-length enumeration or a mere normalization check.
